demand_drivers.title: Mdna (RHP)
demand_drivers.body:
- Global e-waste management market projected to reach USD 244.6 billion by 2032 at a 15.7% CAGR; India's e-waste sector projected to grow faster, at 25% CAGR.
- Critical Mineral Mission (Union Budget 2025-26) creates a policy tailwind for precious-metal and rare-earth recovery, including customs duty exemptions on 25 critical minerals.
- E-Waste Management Rules 2022 mandate stricter EPR compliance, directly driving demand for Ecoreco's recycling solutions.
- Precious metal recovery expected to deliver double-digit growth and carries higher EBITDA margins than traditional recycling.
- ITAD and refurbishment provide steady margins with lower capital intensity; EPR compliance generates stable fee-based income supporting operating leverage.
- Only 17% of e-waste is currently recycled through formal global channels, leaving a structural gap that favors formal recyclers.
- Ecoreco anticipates rapid organic revenue growth over the next three years from precious/rare-earth metal recovery scaling, ITAD & data-destruction demand, and long-term EPR contracts.
- Informal-sector competition for e-waste collection, since generators often prefer selling to the informal sector for higher monetary value, is cited as a threat to formal recyclers' feedstock.
- Revenue growth in FY2025-26 was supported by new client acquisitions under EPR contracts.
- EPR Compliance & Reverse Logistics generates annuitized revenue through long-term contracts with OEMs and brands.

capex_expansion.title: Expansion (RHP)
capex_expansion.body: During FY2025-26 Ecoreco invested in capacity expansion for rare earth and precious metal recovery, expanded the SmartER — Recycling on Wheels mobile collection fleet to deepen collection reach and secure feedstock, and built out digital platforms (barcoding, traceability) for compliance and client transparency. The year's highlights included commissioning of precious metal recovery lines aligned with the Critical Mineral Mission. Continued capex is planned to focus on lithium-ion battery recycling and advanced collection infrastructure.

moat.title: Strengths (RHP)
moat.body:
- licence/regulatory: certified compliance recycler positioned to capture EPR-driven demand — evidence: certifications include R2v3, ISO, NAID, TERRA, MRAI membership
- integration: fully integrated e-waste value chain from collection to material recovery — evidence: business model covers collection, secure data destruction, refurbishment, material recovery and remarketing — against it: informal-sector competitors capture e-waste generators who prefer selling for higher monetary value than to compliant recyclers

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- Informal sector competition impacts collection efficiency, constraining feedstock access for the formal recycler.
- All categories of e-waste generators prefer to sell e-waste to the informal sector for higher monetary value rather than to compliant recyclers who apply higher environmental standards, directly limiting Ecoreco's feedstock supply.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Deepen collection reach and secure feedstock through the SmartER mobile recycling fleet.
- Scale precious metal and rare earth metal recovery out of black mass facilities.
- Expand into lithium-ion battery recycling aligned with EV adoption trends.
- Grow EPR compliance and reverse-logistics business through long-term contracts with OEMs and brands.
- Pursue global partnerships for technology and best practices while retaining Indian-market-adapted leadership.
- Invest in digital platforms (barcoding, traceability) for compliance and client transparency.
